newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan gasoline retail prices slip to new low -- IEE.
newsitem.headline: Japan gasoline retail prices slip to new low -- IEE.

text.p: Japan's retail gasoline prices averaged 103 yen a litre as of July 14, the lowest level since the weekly price survey was initiated in 1990, the Institute of Energy Economics (IEE) said on Wednesday.
"It's fierce competition among retailers (that has pushed the price down)," an IEE official said.
Retail gasoline prices in Japan have been falling sharply since April amid cut-throat price wars at the pump, surpassing declines in wholesale gasoline prices.
The average gasoline price was 107 yen a litre in early April, according to IEE data.

With gasoline priced at 103 yen per litre, profit margins for most service stations are believed to have sunk below the 15-yen-per-litre level, which is widely considered a break-even point, oil product traders said.
